story: One Federal Register notice consolidated three things at once, and the objection on the record against the AI piece is the same objection as against the rest of it.
rule: A claim ships only if a primary government page or the funder's own page was personally fetched and the value read on it. Trade press alone does not carry a claim. Arithmetic on two verified fields is labelled derived and never presented as a published figure. A 403 is UNVERIFIED and the claim is CUT, not softened.

claims.on_screen: 91 FR 47241  ·  JULY 28TH 2026  ·  NOTICE OF FINAL ISSUANCE
claims.spoken: Ninety one Federal Register forty seven thousand two hundred forty one, published July twenty eighth.
claims.note: Federal Register API record
claims.verbatim_source: field: citation = "91 FR 47241", publication_date = "2026-07-28", action = "Notice of Final Issuance."

claims.on_screen: 32 SUBMISSIONS OF PUBLIC COMMENT
claims.spoken: Thirty two submissions of public comment.
claims.note: Federal Register full text
claims.verbatim_source: "ANA received and considered comments from 32 submissions."

claims.on_screen: ANA CONFIRMS THAT SEDS HAS EVOLVED AND EAGLE SIGNIFIES THIS EVOLVEMENT
claims.spoken: The agency's own words. A N A confirms that SEDS has evolved, and EAGLE signifies this evolvement.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, ANA response voice
claims.verbatim_source: "ANA confirms that SEDS has evolved, and EAGLE signifies this evolvement."
claims.requires: ANA never uses the word 'replace' in its own response voice. Do not put it in the agency's mouth.

claims.on_screen: THE INSTITUTE WILL COMPLEMENT NOT REPLACE BROADER SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT EFFORTS
claims.spoken: The Institute will complement, not replace, broader social and economic development efforts.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, on the AI3 Action Institute
claims.verbatim_source: "The Institute will complement--not replace--broader social and economic development efforts."
claims.requires: THIS KILLS THE FRAMING THAT AI3 REPLACED SEDS. EAGLE is the successor. AI3 is an additional award.

claims.on_screen: COMMENTERS RAISED  ·  OPPORTUNITY COSTS  ·  INDIGENOUS DATA SOVEREIGNTY  ·  CENTRALIZED PROGRAM DESIGN  ·  TRIBAL READINESS
claims.spoken: Commenters raised concerns about opportunity costs, Indigenous data sovereignty, centralized program design, and Tribal readiness.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, comments on the AI3 Action Institute
claims.verbatim_source: "some commenters raised concerns regarding \"opportunity costs, Indigenous data sovereignty, centralized program design, Tribal readiness\""
claims.requires: Attribute to commenters. The notice names no commenter, so no organization may be named.

claims.on_screen: AI3 ACTION INSTITUTE  ·  ONE AWARD  ·  FLOOR 2,500,000  ·  CLOSES AUGUST 27TH 2026
claims.spoken: The A I three Action Institute. One award, nationwide, closing August twenty seventh.
claims.note: agency notice of funding opportunity
claims.verbatim_source: field: Award Floor = "$2,500,000", Award Ceiling = "$3,500,000", Total Program Funding = "$3,500,000", Expected Number of Awards = "1", Close Date = "August 27, 2026". The ceiling equalling the whole program funding is the arithmetic confirmation that this is a single national award.

claims.on_screen: EAGLE  ·  24 MILLION DOLLARS  ·  31 AWARDS  ·  COST SHARING REQUIRED
claims.spoken: EAGLE. Twenty four million dollars. Thirty one awards. Cost sharing required.
claims.note: agency notice of funding opportunity
claims.verbatim_source: field: Total Program Funding = "$24,000,000", Expected Number of Awards = "31", Award Floor = "$300,000", Award Ceiling = "$1,000,000", Cost Sharing/Matching = "Yes"
claims.requires: Do NOT say '24 million over three years'. The page does not attach the three year qualifier to that figure.

claims.on_screen: SEDS ALASKA  ·  FY2025  ·  2,000,000  ·  3 AWARDS  ·  FLOOR 100,000  ·  CEILING 900,000
claims.spoken: SEDS Alaska. Fiscal year twenty twenty five. Two million dollars, three awards. It closed July twenty second, twenty twenty five.
claims.note: agency notice of funding opportunity, the last SEDS-Alaska competition
claims.verbatim_source: field: Opportunity Title = "Social and Economic Development Strategies for Alaska-SEDS-AK", Total Program Funding = "$2,000,000", Expected Number of Awards = "3", Award Floor = "$100,000", Award Ceiling = "$900,000", Close Date = "July 22, 2025"

claims.on_screen: FOR FY2026 THERE ARE THREE ANA OPPORTUNITIES AND NONE IS ALASKA SPECIFIC
claims.spoken: For fiscal year twenty twenty six there are three A N A opportunities, and none of them is Alaska specific.
claims.note: grants.gov search performed 2026-08-12, corroborated by the Federal Register naming the same three
claims.verbatim_source: LABELLED NON-QUOTATION, this is a search finding: grants.gov returns exactly three FY2026 ANA opportunities, AI3 (NAI-0035), EAGLE (NEG-0120) and NCNTTA (NTA-0038). The Federal Register notice names the same three.

claims.on_screen: COMMENTERS NAMED THE POTENTIAL LOSS OF AN ALASKA SPECIFIC FUNDING OPPORTUNITY
claims.spoken: Commenters named the potential loss of an Alaska specific funding opportunity, and the possibility that Alaska Tribes could face new barriers competing under a new notice.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, ANA's summary of comments
claims.verbatim_source: "Multiple commenters raised concerns regarding the replacement of SEDS-AK with EAGLE, including the potential loss of an Alaska-specific funding opportunity and the possibility that Alaska Tribes could face new barriers in competing for funding under a new NOFO."

claims.on_screen: THE EAGLE IDEAS PROJECT AREA CARRIES FORWARD THE SPIRIT OF ALASKAN SELF DETERMINATION
claims.spoken: The EAGLE IDEAS project area carries forward the spirit of Alaskan self determination.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, ANA's answer to the Alaska objection
claims.verbatim_source: "The EAGLE IDEAS project area carries forward the spirit of Alaskan self-determination."

claims.on_screen: FOUR ASSISTANCE CONTRACTS CONSOLIDATED INTO ONE
claims.spoken: Four training and technical assistance contracts consolidated into one cooperative agreement.
claims.note: Federal Register full text
claims.verbatim_source: "The consolidation of ANA's four TTA contracts into a single cooperative agreement will streamline operations and strengthen program support."

claims.on_screen: A COMMENTER SAID IT EQUATES TO A REDUCTION OF MORE THAN 70 PERCENT IN REGIONAL STAFFING CAPACITY
claims.spoken: One commenter said it equates to a reduction of more than seventy percent in regional staffing capacity.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, a comment quoted by ANA
claims.verbatim_source: "the proposed ceiling level of $3.1M over three years for a single NCNTTA cooperative agreement represents a substantial consolidation of resources and equates to a reduction of more than 70 percent in regional staffing capacity."
claims.requires: MUST be paired with c14. The film may not air one side of this.

claims.on_screen: THE AGENCY ANSWERED 3.1 MILLION DOLLARS PER FISCAL YEAR
claims.spoken: The agency answered that the funding level is three point one million per fiscal year.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, ANA response
claims.verbatim_source: "The funding level, which is 3.1 million per fiscal year, is intended to support a coordinated national technical assistance approach"
claims.requires: The commenter says over three years, the agency says per fiscal year. THE RECORD DOES NOT RESOLVE IT. The film must show both and say it is unresolved.

claims.on_screen: NSF 2433241  ·  RAISE  ·  380000 DOLLARS  ·  UAA
claims.spoken: National Science Foundation award two four three three two four one. Rural A I Solutions and Engagement. Three hundred eighty thousand dollars, to the University of Alaska Anchorage.
claims.note: NSF award API record, fetched by the orchestrator
claims.verbatim_source: field: awardee = "UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA ANCHORAGE", estimatedTotalAmt = "380000", expDate = "07/31/2027", title = "Rural AI Solutions and Engagement (RAISE)"

claims.on_screen: TWELVE ALASKA ORGANIZATIONS ASKED  ·  FOUR WERE FUNDED
claims.spoken: Twelve Alaska organizations asked. Four were funded.
claims.note: funder's own page; the four funded projects are listed on the awardee page
claims.verbatim_source: LABELLED NON-QUOTATION, this is a count off the funder's own two pages: the statement-of-need page lists the submitted community proposals and the awardee page names four funded projects.
claims.requires: If the twelve cannot be recounted item by item at build time, drop the twelve and say only that four were funded.

claims.on_screen: NOME JOINT UTILITIES SYSTEM  ·  PREDICTING THERMAL CONDUCTIVITY OF WARMING PERMAFROST
claims.spoken: Nome Joint Utilities System asked about predicting the thermal conductivity of warming permafrost.
claims.note: funder's own awardee page, fetched by the orchestrator
claims.verbatim_source: "Predicting Thermal Conductivity of Warming Permafrost for Hazards Estimation using Machine Learning" paired on the page with "Community Partner: Nome Joint Utilities System"

claims.on_screen: VILLAGE OF ALAKANUK TRIBE  ·  AI FOR RURAL COMMUNITY TRANSFORMATION AND INFRASTRUCTURE COORDINATION
claims.spoken: The Village of Alakanuk Tribe asked for A I for rural community transformation and infrastructure coordination.
claims.note: funder's own awardee page, fetched by the orchestrator
claims.verbatim_source: "ARCTIC: AI for Rural Community Transformation and Infrastructure Coordination" paired on the page with "Community Partner: Village of Alakanuk Tribe"

claims.on_screen: ANY ALASKAN ORGANIZATION OUTSIDE OF THE UNIVERSITY
claims.spoken: Eligibility was any Alaskan organization outside of the university.
claims.note: funder's own program page
claims.verbatim_source: "any Alaskan organization outside of the university, including large or small businesses, Alaska native organizations, K-12 education, government entities, non-profits, or UA research center"

claims.on_screen: AUGUST 7TH 2026  ·  CONSORTIUM LIBRARY ROOM 307
claims.spoken: August seventh, twenty twenty six, in Consortium Library room three oh seven.
claims.note: funder's own workshop page, fetched by the orchestrator
claims.verbatim_source: field: "August 7, 2026, 10:15 AM - 1:30 PM", "Library 307", "UAA/APU Consortium Library"

claims.on_screen: 229 FEDERALLY RECOGNIZED TRIBES IN ALASKA
claims.spoken: Alaska has two hundred twenty nine federally recognized tribes.
claims.note: BIA Alaska Regional Office, which STATES the number rather than requiring a count
claims.verbatim_source: "More than 180,000 Tribal members make up the 229 Federally Recognized Tribes under the jurisdiction of the Alaska Regional Office"
claims.requires: Cite the BIA page. NEVER derive this by counting the Federal Register list, which is not numbered; a first fetch fabricated a count of it during validation.

claims.on_screen: ALASKA NATIVE COMMUNITIES WILL REMAIN ELIGIBLE ACROSS EAGLE PROJECT AREAS
claims.spoken: Alaska Native communities stay eligible.
claims.note: Federal Register full text, re-fetched 2026-08-12 specifically to source this line after panel round 2 found it carried no claim id. The film's even-handedness card rested on nothing; it rests on this now.
claims.verbatim_source: "Alaska Native communities will remain eligible across EAGLE project areas."
claims.requires: This sources ELIGIBILITY and nothing else. It does not license any claim about who can realistically LEAD or WIN an award, which is the inference the round-2 script made and which is now cut.

claims.on_screen: (cut) WHAT IS IT PAID TO PRODUCE / A LIST OF WHERE AI COULD HELP
claims.spoken: (cut) So what is the institute paid to produce? A list.
claims.note: KILLED 2026-08-12 after panel round 2. This was the pivot the whole back half of the film turned on and it carried no claim id. The Federal Register full text was re-fetched and asked directly for any statement of the AI3 Institute's deliverable, output, roadmap, assessment, inventory, report or scope of work. ABSENT. The notice states only a purpose, supporting informed community decision-making, and that the Institute will address ethical, practical and governance considerations. Nothing says it produces a list. The characterization was the run's own and it is cut, not softened.
claims.verbatim_source: NOT FOUND. The document contains no statement of the Institute's deliverable.
claims.requires: Never restore this line without a primary page that states the deliverable in its own words.

claims.on_screen: (cut) 8 STILL HOLDING A LIST NOBODY PUBLISHED
claims.spoken: (cut) Eight still hold a list nobody published.
claims.note: KILLED 2026-08-12 after panel round 2, and it is contradicted by c16's own verbatim note, which records that the statement-of-need page LISTS the submitted community proposals. If that page lists them, the eight asks are published and the line is simply false. It was also the film's primary open-loop payoff, planted at 14.3s and paid at 102.12s, which is exactly the kind of line that gets written for its shape rather than its truth. Replaced with the fact c16 does carry: eight went unfunded.
claims.verbatim_source: Contradicted by c16: "the statement-of-need page lists the submitted community proposals".
claims.requires: The unfunded eight are UNFUNDED, not unpublished. Do not conflate the two again.

claims.on_screen: (cut) AI COMES WITH A VENDOR CONTRACT
claims.spoken: (cut) and A I comes with a vendor contract
claims.note: KILLED 2026-08-12 after panel round 5. It carried no claim id and it was LOAD-BEARING: the film's entire steelman at 63.68s rested on it. That is the same failure mode that killed c23, a characterization the run made, delivered with the authority of the record. Nothing in the notice says an AI award comes with a vendor contract. The steelman is rebuilt on c12, which is ANA's own sentence about consolidating four TTA contracts into a single agreement.
claims.verbatim_source: NOT FOUND. No primary page states this.
claims.requires: Do not restore without a primary page that says it in its own words.

killed.claim: Any Alaska Federation of Natives quotation
killed.why: Sole source nativenewsonline.net returns HTTP 403, reproduced twice. The quote exists only as a search-engine snippet. The Federal Register names no commenter. NO AFN QUOTE MAY APPEAR.
No source. acf.gov/ana/programs/seds returns HTTP 403. The film may not state how long the program ran, not thirty years and not any other figure.

killed.claim: The AI3 Action Institute replaced SEDS or SEDS-Alaska
killed.why: REFUTED BY THE PRIMARY DOCUMENT. ANA writes the Institute will 'complement--not replace--broader social and economic development efforts'. EAGLE is the successor. AI3 is an additional award.

killed.claim: The AI3 project period in years
killed.why: Not stated on the grants.gov record. The three year period belongs to EAGLE only and may not be carried across.
The page does not attach the three year qualifier to the 24 million figure. State them as two separate facts.

killed.claim: Any claim that a UAA mini-grant tool works
killed.why: No result, finding, accuracy figure or deployment is published for any of the four projects. No per-project dollar figure exists publicly either.

killed.claim: Any assertion that an Alaskan has been denied a grant
killed.why: No AI3 award has been made and no EAGLE award is announced. Asserting harm already done would be false.

cultural_flags: ANA never writes 'replaced' in its own response voice. It writes 'evolved' and 'transition'. Putting 'replace' in the agency's mouth misquotes a federal agency.
The Alaska-specific objection is ON THE RECORD as commenters' words, not the film's inference. Attribute it to commenters. The notice names none, so name no organization.

Indigenous data sovereignty was raised directly against the AI3 Institute. A film about an AI program for Native communities that omits that objection omits the load-bearing critique the record contains.

The AI3 eligibility pool is WIDER than tribes: Native CDFIs, Urban Indian Centers, Tribal Colleges, and Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander serving agencies are all in it. One award against a field that broad.

Do not render Alaska Native villages as passive recipients. The eligibility text is a list of Alaska Native institutions with legal standing as applicants. What changed is the competition's shape, not their standing.

Federally recognized tribes, ANCSA village corporations, Alaska Native regional corporations, nonprofit tribal consortia and advocacy organizations are legally distinct and none speaks for the others.

NEVER draw any Alaska Native person, community, tribal government or the Village of Alakanuk Tribe as a characterized object with a face. Characterized-object treatment is reserved for the paperwork and the programs.
on_screen_numbers_are_illustrative_note: Every figure on screen is quoted from a federal notice of funding opportunity, the Federal Register full text, or the NSF award record, and is current as of 2026-08-12. No figure is modelled, projected or estimated by this film.
